Cherokee Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Neches River near Alto.

* WHEN...From Friday morning to Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, Boat ramps and picnic areas near the river
will begin to flood. Ranchers should move cattle and equipment near
the river to higher ground.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 4.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage Friday
morning to a crest of 16.4 feet early Saturday morning. It will
then fall below flood stage late Saturday evening.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

walking near riverbanks. Turn around, don't drown when encountering
flooded roads. Most flood deaths occur in vehicles.

through flooded areas.

address into your favorite web browser URL bar:
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/SHV

floor of a sturdy building. Avoid windows. If you are outdoors, in a
mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter
and protect yourself from flying debris.

properties.description:
TORGRR

The National Weather Service in Grand Rapids has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
Northeastern Ingham County in south central Michigan...

* Until 330 PM EDT.

* At 306 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located 6 miles southwest of Fowlerville, moving southeast at
50 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed.
Damage to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree
damage is likely.

* This tornadic thunderstorm will remain over mainly rural areas of
northeastern Ingham County, including the following locations...
Bell Oak and Webberville.
properties.instruction:
TAKE COVER NOW! Move to a basement or an interior room on the lowest
floor of a sturdy building. Avoid windows. If you are outdoors, in a
mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter
and protect yourself from flying debris.
